📡 Iranian President calls for stronger deterrence as new IRGC leadership takes office

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has congratulated Major General Ahmad Vahidi and Major General Mostafa Izadi on their appointments as Chief Commander and Deputy Commander of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC), respectively, stressing the need to strengthen Iran’s deterrence, national cohesion and security readiness.

In separate messages issued Tuesday, Pezeshkian described the IRGC as a significant institution in defending Islamic Republic of Iran and safeguarding national security, while emphasizing the importance of strengthening the country’s deterrence capabilities, scientific and technological capacity, as well as national cohesion.
​
Addressing Vahidi, Pezeshkian said his appointment by Leader of the Islamic Revolution and Commander-in-Chief Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei reflected his competence, judgment, insight and longstanding efforts in defending Iran.
​
Pezeshkian said the IRGC had been an important institution in defending the country and protecting national security throughout the history of the Islamic Revolution.
​
He added that leading the organization, particularly under current sensitive circumstances, requires experience, courage, foresight and a precise understanding of national interests and regional conditions.
​
President Pezeshkian said Vahidi’s experience in various military and managerial positions, particularly in the defense sector, would provide an important foundation for leading the IRGC in a new phase of its missions.
​
Pezeshkian also identified strengthening deterrence, improving scientific and technological capabilities, utilizing the scientific and spiritual potential of young people and experts, maintaining readiness to defend Iran, and contributing to national cohesion as essential elements of national power.
​
Turning to Izadi’s appointment as the Deputy Commander of the IRGC, Pezeshkian said his experience and commitment in various military and defense fields represented a valuable asset for the IRGC and a reliable foundation for his new responsibilities.
​
He said the position of deputy commander requires not only experience and managerial capabilities but also a detailed understanding of defense and security developments and the ability to connect past experience with future requirements.
​
Pezeshkian noted that defense and security issues are increasingly linked to knowledge, technology and rapid changes in the surrounding environment.
​
He said using the capabilities of young specialists, transferring experience between generations and strengthening scientific and technological capabilities could further enhance Iran’s defense capabilities for future challenges.
​
Pezeshkian expressed hope that Izadi would use the IRGC’s capabilities to strengthen its readiness, cohesion and effectiveness and contribute to protecting Iran’s security and interests.
